basics.name: Gear type references: KHK (Kohara Gear Industry) Gear Technical Reference and Gear Knowledge pages, and SDP/SI 'Elements of Metric Gear Technology'
basics.url: KHK: https://khkgears.net/new/gear_knowledge/gear_technical_reference/ (table of contents), with https://khkgears.net/new/gear_knowledge/ (Gear Knowledge hub), https://khkgears.net/new/gear_knowledge/gear_technical_reference/gear_types_terminology.html , https://khkgears.net/new/gear_knowledge/gear_technical_reference/gear-trains.html , https://khkgears.net/new/gear_knowledge/gear_technical_reference/gear_systems.html , https://khkgears.net/new/gear_knowledge/Types_and_Mechanisms_of_Gear_Reducers.html and https://khkgears.net/new/gear_knowledge/gear-nomenclature/ . SDP/SI: official page https://sdp-si.com/resources/elements-of-metric-gear-technology/index.php and PDF https://www.sdp-si.com/D805/D805_PDFS/Technical/8050T017.pdf appeared in search but sdp-si.com returned a bot-check page and could not be opened [uncertain]; the full text was read from a third-party mirror, https://idoc.tips/elements-of-metric-gear-technology-pdf-free.html
basics.resource_type: PDF design guide (manufacturers' gear engineering handbooks, published as web pages and PDFs)

All Rights Reserved'; KHK's reducer-types article is itself reproduced with permission from a Japanese book (Japan Institute of Plant Maintenance, Shinpan Gensokuki No Hon, 2008). SDP/SI: 'No part of this publication may be reproduced in any form or by any means without prior written permission of the company.' Link and cite only; do not copy figures
basics.language: English (KHK is a Japanese company; the reference follows JIS/ISO terms; KHK also runs Japanese-language sites [uncertain]). SDP/SI is English (US company, metric focus)
basics.year: KHK web pages show copyright 2021 and a new magnetic-gear banner, so still updated in 2026; KHK 'ABCs of Gears - A' PDF last modified 26 May 2020 (server header); the reference's content comes from KHK's printed catalogue technical section, which is older [uncertain]. SDP/SI Elements of Metric Gear Technology is the technical section of SDP/SI's printed catalogue (D805 series) and dates from the 1990s-2000s [uncertain]
basics.access_barrier: none for KHK; SDP/SI site sits behind a JavaScript bot-check (Sucuri) that ordinary browsers pass automatically [uncertain]
basics.image_license: Same as text: all rights reserved. KHK uses clean rendered gear images (webp) for each gear type and line drawings for gear trains and planetary systems; SDP/SI uses line drawings and tables
basics.authority_level: manufacturer (two established gear makers; KHK is a Japanese gear maker, SDP/SI is Stock Drive Products / Sterling Instrument, part of Designatronics). SDP/SI credits KHK for the material and Dr George Michalec (Stevens Institute of Technology) as a contributor

coverage.covers: Gear types and gear trains in depth. Types: spur gear, gear rack, internal gear, helical gear, helical rack, double helical (herringbone), straight / spiral / Zerol bevel gears, miter gears, worm gear pair, screw (crossed helical) gear, face gear, enveloping (hourglass) worm, hypoid gear (about 15 types). Gear trains: single-stage (with rotation direction for external, internal, bevel and worm meshes), rack and pinion, two-stage, idler, planetary (2K-H) with planetary / solar / star arrangements, hypocycloid (small tooth-difference internal gearing, e.g. 30:31 for 30:1), constrained (closed-loop) gear systems. KHK's reducer article adds gearbox families: parallel, orthogonal (bevel), skew (worm, hypoid) and coaxial (simple planetary, differential planetary, eccentric planetary, elastic planetary), with the Cyclo (cycloidal) reducer explained in detail. Plus involute geometry, profile shift, tooth thickness, backlash and anti-backlash methods, accuracy grades, materials and heat treatment, strength (bending and pitting), plastic gear design, forces, lubrication, damage and noise. KHK also has an 86-term gear nomenclature glossary and pages on magnetic gears and couplings. SDP/SI has 21 sections of about 230 pages (T-7 to T-232)
coverage.organisation: Textbook order by engineering topic (types and terms, trains, involute profile, dimension calculations, tooth thickness, backlash, accuracy, mounting, materials, strength, plastic gears, forces, lubrication, damage, noise, gear systems). Gear types are classified by how the two shafts sit: parallel, intersecting, or neither (skew). That shaft-arrangement question is a good plain-language starting point, but the rest assumes you want to calculate gear dimensions, so beginners will get lost after the first two chapters
coverage.scope_match: medium: the best authority for gear types and gear-train types (which the project wants), with clear shaft-arrangement classification and planetary, hypocycloid and cycloidal reducers, but most of the content is detailed calculation for standard involute gears; it does not cover strain-wave (harmonic) drives, differentials as a type, belts and chains, or non-gear connections
coverage.taxonomy_used: By axis orientation, 3 groups plus extras: parallel axes gears, intersecting axes gears, nonparallel-and-nonintersecting axes gears, plus 'other special gears' (face gear, enveloping worm, hypoid). Gear trains by stages (single, two-stage) and by speed ratio (increasing, equal, reducing). Gear reducers by shaft position (parallel, orthogonal, skew, coaxial = 4 groups), with coaxial split into simple, differential, eccentric and elastic planetary
coverage.example_types: spur gear; gear rack (rack and pinion); internal (ring) gear; helical gear; double helical (herringbone) gear; straight bevel gear; spiral bevel gear; Zerol bevel gear; miter gear; face (crown) gear; worm gear pair (self-locking at low lead angle); enveloping (hourglass) worm; screw (crossed helical) gear; hypoid gear; idler gear; planetary (2K-H epicyclic) gear system; hypocycloid mechanism (one-tooth-difference internal gearing); constrained (closed-loop) gear system; Cyclo (cycloidal) speed reducer; eccentric / differential / elastic planetary reducers; anti-backlash split gear (spring-loaded); magnetic gear and magnetic coupling (non-contact, slips under overload)
coverage.making_methods: General mechanical engineering and gearbox design; machined and moulded gears; KHK and SDP/SI both cover plastic gears (nylon, Duracon/acetal, moulded vs cut), which is useful for 3D-printed gears, but neither mentions 3D printing
coverage.item_count: About 15 gear types and about 8 gear-train or reducer types; KHK Gear Technical Reference has 17 chapters plus extra pages (anti-backlash gears, gear design, gear pump); KHK glossary has 86 terms; SDP/SI has 21 sections, about 230 pages
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: Gear trains/gearboxes: yes, strong (single and multi-stage trains, idlers, planetary with three fixed-member cases and worked ratios, hypocycloid, cycloidal reducer, worm reducers up to 1:100 per stage, bevel and hypoid reducers). Self-locking: yes (worm gears at small lead angle; KHK notes true self-locking is hard to guarantee; SDP/SI gives the conditions for worm self-locking). Torque-limiting: only indirectly, via KHK's magnetic gears and couplings that slip under overload. Backlash removal with springs (dynamic methods: split gear halves forced apart, spring-closed centre distance). One-way/ratchet, indexing/detent (no Geneva or intermittent gears seen), over-centre, hand-release, compliant, print-in-place, powered connectors, adhesives: not covered
coverage.entry_structure: Per gear type: name, rendered image, figure number, 2-4 sentence description with pros and cons, efficiency range. Per chapter: definitions, formulas, tables of symbols and worked numerical examples (e.g. za = 16, zb = 16, zc = 48 gives ratio 4)
coverage.audience_level: professional and undergraduate (gear designers); KHK's 'ABCs of Gears - A', 'First step of mechanism design using gears' and 'Gear Tips' pages are aimed at beginners

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: medium: the gear-type pages are short, well illustrated and sorted by a simple question (how are the shafts arranged?), and KHK has explicit beginner primers, but the technical reference quickly becomes formula-heavy with ISO/JIS symbols and no plain-English layer
usefulness.has_images: yes: KHK has clear rendered images of every gear type and neat line drawings of gear trains, planetary and cycloidal reducers; SDP/SI has black-and-white line drawings and many tables
usefulness.has_animations: no animations or videos seen on the pages opened
usefulness.gaps: No harmonic / strain-wave drive, differential, belt, chain or ratchet pages in the reference (KHK's reducer article only names 'elastic planetary' and 'differential planetary' groups); nothing on 3D-printed gears (clearances, printable tooth sizes, herringbone for FDM); no function-first selector ('I need a big reduction in a small space'); maths-heavy after the first chapter; SDP/SI could not be opened on its own site here [uncertain]
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: yes for KHK: stable per-topic pages, e.g. https://khkgears.net/new/gear_knowledge/gear_technical_reference/gear_types_terminology.html (gear types), https://khkgears.net/new/gear_knowledge/gear_technical_reference/gear_systems.html (planetary, hypocycloid), https://khkgears.net/new/gear_knowledge/Types_and_Mechanisms_of_Gear_Reducers.html (worm, cycloidal reducers), and 86 glossary pages such as https://khkgears.net/new/gear_knowledge/gear-nomenclature/ . SDP/SI is one long PDF split into section pages on its own site, so links would be per section [uncertain]
usefulness.reusable_data: not reusable beyond linking and citing facts (all rights reserved; SDP/SI forbids reproduction without written permission). Scrape-only HTML and PDF
usefulness.maintained: KHK: live and updated (new magnetic gears and couplings pages; khkgears.net and khkgears2.net catalogue). SDP/SI: live site per search results, but blocked here; the text is widely mirrored (idoc.tips, academia.edu, Scribd, FlipHTML5) [uncertain]
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: (1) Use the shaft-arrangement question as a flow-chart branch: 'Are the input and output shafts parallel, crossing at an angle, or skewed / offset?' then show the gear types for each. (2) Give each gear type an efficiency range (spur/helical 98-99.5%, bevel 98-99%, screw 70-95%, worm 30-90%) so beginners see the cost of worm drives. (3) Show rotation direction per mesh type (external reverses, internal keeps direction, worm depends on helix hand). (4) Use KHK's three planetary cases (ring fixed, sun fixed, carrier fixed) with one worked ratio each. (5) Typical ratio ranges per reducer family (parallel 1:1-1:7 per stage, worm 1:5-1:100, Cyclo up to 1:119 per stage) as quick guidance. (6) A short linked glossary like KHK's gear nomenclature
usefulness.design_rules_given: Yes: efficiency ranges per gear type; single-stage ratio ranges per reducer family (parallel 1/1-1/7 one stage, 1/10-1/30 two stage; straight bevel 1:1 and 1:2 under 1000 rpm; spiral bevel up to 1:6; worm 1:5-1:100, and worm efficiency 60-95% for lead angles 5-40 degrees; Cyclo about 98% per stage, up to 1:119 one stage); worm housing temperature limit about 90 C with mineral oil; planetary tooth-count conditions (coaxial, even spacing, adjacent-planet clearance); full strength, backlash, accuracy (ISO/JIS/AGMA) and plastic-gear strength calculations
usefulness.generator_or_parametric: No geometry generators; formulas and tables only. KHK mentions planned gear calculation software and offers CAD downloads for its stock gears in its catalogue [uncertain]
usefulness.file_formats: HTML pages and PDF handbooks (KHK 'ABCs of Gears' PDFs; SDP/SI PDF)
usefulness.terminology_value: high: authoritative, ISO/JIS-aligned English names and symbols for gear types and gear geometry (module, profile shift, Zerol, hypoid, screw gear = crossed helical gear, enveloping worm, 2K-H planetary, sun gear, planet carrier, idler), with an 86-term glossary; no translations in the English pages
usefulness.decision_support: Tables that compare gear types by axis arrangement and efficiency, and reducer families by ratio and characteristics; KHK's separate 'Selecting gears' page and step-by-step design procedure series; no interactive selector or flow chart
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: SDP/SI states that KHK (Kohara Gear) provided the material, so the two overlap heavily (same chapter order, the same gear-type table and planetary/constrained gear-system sections); treat them as one source family and cite KHK as the original. KHK's reducer article is translated from a JMA Consultants book (2008). Overlaps with RoyMech gear pages, Machinery's Handbook, and Wikipedia gear articles [uncertain]
